feedback: I enjoy surveys and making extra money. No questions.

I almost always ignore race and personality factors, as their background and emotional patterns mostly do not determine whether they are reasonable or not. For the rest, I evaluated if the mistakes they make is honest/unavoidable, or if it was entirely avoidable and/or their own wrongdoing.
I thought about what I would do in the situation as I think of myself as a reasonable person. I thought about the actions taken and whether or not it was "fair" that the person did them.
I tried to be understanding that sometimes things happen and not to judge each person too harshly.
i just went with my gut i mean does of these thing are not great thing to do i do get it that it happen but still
I just thought of them as an ordinary person and what they should or should not do in each scenario.
A few of the negative statements threw me a little (the double negative NOT NOT), but otherwise everything seemed easy to understand.

Some assumption of how the law would see a situation sometimes influenced me, such as the driving example where the driver was distracted by his phone and sideswiped a biker. I think in the eyes of the law the driver would be at fault, no matter why he was distracted. A lot of the other examples I did not have an obvious legal president to compare to.
I considered each case individually. No comments.
i tried to look at the problem rationally. the fact that you might do something against whether you should.
i put myself in the situation.
The situation itself as well as their age and the emotional factor.
If the person behaved the way I think most people in the situation would behave, then I view it as reasonable. Sometimes it also would be more reasonable to take further action.

I thought about what I would do as a short hand to determine the reasonability of the person in the situation. If they did something nonsensical, then that would be something I would not have done, and something no reasonable person would do.
I weighed all info and decided based on what was provided. Very interesting study, thank you!
What I thought influenced me.
I considered the severity of the situations and/or actions and whether or not it would be a normal reaction given the circumstances.
I considered what would be reasonable knowing what I think and based on law
In many cases people's actions were understandable even if they led to poor outcomes.

I used the reasonable person standard. If there was a case where someone had an obligation to act a certain way I took that into consideration, such as if someone was driving I considered that they had an obligation to drive carefully and not recklessly.

I thought about what I would feel were best practice in these situations. The PTSD one was harder because it's tough to know how you'd behave with it. In most cases, I picked choices I felt were dangerous and marked those.
I just thought about myself in the person's shoes.

The consequences and scenarios themselves influenced how I responded.
I tried to think logically. Was someone doing something wrong or were these normal things to do in those situations?

Kind of a general question.  My response varied with the situation. Except damn, I COULD NOT say that the battered woman was unreasonable for smoking her husband, even if he was NOT an immediate threat to her life.  I thought shooting him was a pretty reasonable reaction, under the circumstances.

I tried to find a single point, if any, where something unreasonable happened. Like the guy who checked his text while driving--it was unreasonable to do so, but not "unreasonable" per se to hit the cyclist once he had already done so.
What I believed was right and wrong in a situation, or what I believed was a normal reaction to something.

The key factors that influenced my decisions were based on if the individuals in question were able to make a conscious decision or if they simply had a logic reaction.  I weighed whether a reasonable person would make the same decisions and actions.
Most of the actions were accidents.  I clicked on actions that should have been or not have been done by a normal person.
The information presented. I logically responded without judgement.
Who is at fault.

I tried to answer the questions based on the context of the scenarios. In other words, I tried to consider the extenuating circumstances as much as I could when decided whether or not a reasonable person would have not done something.
I was influenced to respond less negatively if I felt bad for the person or if I felt their actions were justified or understandable.
